question: In connection with the implementation of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, many Polish citizens are expressing concerns about the potential impact of this policy on Poland’s sovereignty, social stability and labour market. Given the current public debate around migration policy, important questions are being raised about the practical application of the Pact on Migration and Asylum and its impact on the social and economic structures of EU Member States. 1.
Can the Commission provide a comprehensive update of the current state of implementation of the Pact on Migration and Asylum in individual Member States, including Poland?
Could the Commission set out how the Pact on Migration and Asylum respects the autonomy of Member States in managing migration flows in line with national priorities and security considerations?

How does the Commission plan to address potential tensions between support for current residents, including EU citizens seeking employment, and the management of newly arrived people under the Pact on Migration and Asylum, especially considering the differing possibilities and preferences of the individual Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.4.2025) The new rules under the Pact on Migration and Asylum will become applicable as of mid2026. Member States are currently working, with the support of the Commission and relevant EU bodies, offices and agencies, on their national implementation plans, setting out the actions and timeline for the implementation of the various instruments under the Pact.

Member States had until 12 December 2024 to establish their plans. The Commission has received almost all plans and will report on the state of play of Pact implementation with indications of next steps.

While the migration management system established by the Pact is based on solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between Member States, the solidarity mechanism is designed to be flexible and able to swiftly adapt to the evolving nature of the migratory challenges.

Each Member State will have a choice on the type of solidarity to be provided (relocations, financial contributions or through alternative solidarity measures such as staff and in-kind support). At the EU level, the Commission has developed a comprehensive approach to migration with clear rights and obligations for third-country nationals.
The Action Plan on integration and inclusion 2021-20271 promotes an integrated approach to third country nationals’ inclusion to prevent and respond to possible social tensions.
1 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and

Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions Action plan on integration and inclusion 2021-2027, COM(2020) 758 final, 24.11.2020 and https://migrant-integration.ec.europa.eu/news/ec-reveals-its-new-actionplan-integration-and-inclusion-2021-2027_en
